[QUERENT] ban on factions 1921

[SYSTEM] The ban on factions was introduced in March 1921 at the [Tenth Congress of the Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks)](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAV8cQYYZ2R8yPak8UKto1FHAlhjfCuKD9NNxkA1xPboisgzzZ_cVf6exLLXiTbu4gaj71DGUj3nE77hyFYBsCXyTytDxJDiyiyneOaXlm4iInj6CjOWiv20VwrwQFXxvZn7tHcmCFbGp_qxw) through the resolution "On Party Unity", proposed by Vladimir Lenin. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHrOzAVDicZfmyVor8fuQUuHvbliUTcdgmguY1gIBJAeHAeylsdH3sdeuysh5csFNFWFthZca7rTqT82VMRCvKEsdsZuk_BupBdbRI-nl63f2hyQ-bH6IvgGy1b-z1NQd8Y5L7WSphUCubJcijlVSi6), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAV8cQYYZ2R8yPak8UKto1FHAlhjfCuKD9NNxkA1xPboisgzzZ_cVf6exLLXiTbu4gaj71DGUj3nE77hyFYBsCXyTytDxJDiyiyneOaXlm4iInj6CjOWiv20VwrwQFXxvZn7tHcmCFbGp_qxw), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHrOzAV3vZFyOBKtrihdd160SsmOYEX90bATrlHwmw6kEavWcECns-jGESt_N1hu1WnQUoEsDxS5LH3M8Y_ZsKziv3m8w21WlPPeRiQ2MGdsssRG1ZBcOtQ0ceQ6BLjagp9tbrA6PA87STJv03mV7PynBQyXjzQ)]
Key Details of the Ban

* The Resolution: Officially titled "On Party Unity", the decree ordered the immediate dissolution of all organized groups and factions within the party that tended to weaken its unity. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHrOzAVg8GhcMLBYLV6JIUKbLCU4Um_hJhdWIe4SPyBFz07-R3qteNEk1tB-CtwaT4bCvf-G97mTS2cLoPt4mxUUiQ8eeY_jNB2ByafsVgjnNf458gct0Vc-YHS2_jYuhn93j2TLORdQuWFli8eSbfr1IE3DXp_AqVGpKE)]
* The Penalty: It authorized the Central Committee to use expulsion from the party as an extreme measure against any members, including its own, who engaged in factional activity. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHrOzAVg8GhcMLBYLV6JIUKbLCU4Um_hJhdWIe4SPyBFz07-R3qteNEk1tB-CtwaT4bCvf-G97mTS2cLoPt4mxUUiQ8eeY_jNB2ByafsVgjnNf458gct0Vc-YHS2_jYuhn93j2TLORdQuWFli8eSbfr1IE3DXp_AqVGpKE)]
* Immediate Targets: It was primarily aimed at suppressing internal opposition groups like the Workers' Opposition (led by figures such as Alexander Shliapnikov and Alexandra Kollontai), who wanted economic control handed over to trade unions rather than the state, as well as the Democratic Centralists. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHrOzAVGXtU4xUJ4-mDW4T2HzN6OE5up2q3R2ZTNaqsnYL8yeqeVsf6L_bqJ2-YK37jHsFFucsZ_rWQQLCOX8pL7uZGL6CqggjnZqoPi-RcINuFikHk5Y8DL3ieW1C6Kuo91O2RhJ1Um6KzYfrumSaO), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEB6zswFbO5lJRzOJwhsQcqU0YqYS0XedOCL5G7IU7N0yGpVgGLENoPABcDhLhqGfDqf-MjRcEnsUQ0PZJFrSye4J5ieZ6a6IpMBmj8N31s8h3b6DkJOz-pfJFlplwkeKsuCqQGmV5pA9FTPc4PgTbJb_2zETklpKtdWC5gPftKzbdybh3pqXwcDYtbjjGMmQ), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHrOzAVDicZfmyVor8fuQUuHvbliUTcdgmguY1gIBJAeHAeylsdH3sdeuysh5csFNFWFthZca7rTqT82VMRCvKEsdsZuk_BupBdbRI-nl63f2hyQ-bH6IvgGy1b-z1NQd8Y5L7WSphUCubJcijlVSi6)]
* Context & Motivation: The ban was passed amid deep economic and political crisis—including the Russian famine, the Kronstadt rebellion, and widespread worker/peasant unrest. Lenin argued that internal dissent and public criticism provided ammunition to foreign and counter-revolutionary enemies. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlgEB6zswFX7h3EV9IDsnpqLsnM9Jq13xO84LZBiErzODFbbIe-CYGGaAzkwtdq73nytGQnbTSuk-ly7dKR5pkircnzjeZHguubZjmkoldbYNJsqpe1_JTr8f3Q82UScrZZ3O20jpFPtDkFCvcaeSduwnTd-r6kEKMGltQ8KUb0fox40b8ZXZ66RHHuezJTFMfmHhTxuuqmk), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHrOzAV3vZFyOBKtrihdd160SsmOYEX90bATrlHwmw6kEavWcECns-jGESt_N1hu1WnQUoEsDxS5LH3M8Y_ZsKziv3m8w21WlPPeRiQ2MGdsssRG1ZBcOtQ0ceQ6BLjagp9tbrA6PA87STJv03mV7PynBQyXjzQ), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAV8cQYYZ2R8yPak8UKto1FHAlhjfCuKD9NNxkA1xPboisgzzZ_cVf6exLLXiTbu4gaj71DGUj3nE77hyFYBsCXyTytDxJDiyiyneOaXlm4iInj6CjOWiv20VwrwQFXxvZn7tHcmCFbGp_qxw), [4](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEB6zswFbO5lJRzOJwhsQcqU0YqYS0XedOCL5G7IU7N0yGpVgGLENoPABcDhLhqGfDqf-MjRcEnsUQ0PZJFrSye4J5ieZ6a6IpMBmj8N31s8h3b6DkJOz-pfJFlplwkeKsuCqQGmV5pA9FTPc4PgTbJb_2zETklpKtdWC5gPftKzbdybh3pqXwcDYtbjjGMmQ)]

Consequences

* End of Internal Debate: It effectively dismantled the Bolshevik tradition of open internal debate, platform voting, and free discussion before reaching a party decision. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEB6zswFWwkbhc0Au6fXV22dJnF9u1AorYteTlzci_2ROfz2oF7XGO2VEc1pjX8stxQv2BVoZVgXZYljJRar519B2MNJq99oZxQoeNXIwV1tvldo_g2Ah8avrH5o0KL08goHTN62JvDIz8oO_-_4af-0gArEO7RnZz-JTun2PC0KSkfHen9GndxJyf9327ymmU), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHrOzAVdarVE1on4CJnns-iUprZOfbTmaIwuN_bUAn1WmD-5HBGHMpCaVpn9TfZaVTrsU_6exDUeXD7RtsZ8KvDeoQJMEiloMrpzQjzzC2ac1GRlcv20URjQ5J2NxAggS_X7oijNemAEJyd6mvA5freREZTF-zlrWxnVOgyog)]
* Path to Stalinism: While conceived by Lenin as an emergency temporary measure, the ban established a precedent. It later provided Joseph Stalin with the institutional mechanism to purge rival political blocs—such as Trotsky's Left Opposition and Bukharin's Right Opposition—under the label of "factionalism". [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEB6zswFWwkbhc0Au6fXV22dJnF9u1AorYteTlzci_2ROfz2oF7XGO2VEc1pjX8stxQv2BVoZVgXZYljJRar519B2MNJq99oZxQoeNXIwV1tvldo_g2Ah8avrH5o0KL08goHTN62JvDIz8oO_-_4af-0gArEO7RnZz-JTun2PC0KSkfHen9GndxJyf9327ymmU), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlgEB6zswFX7h3EV9IDsnpqLsnM9Jq13xO84LZBiErzODFbbIe-CYGGaAzkwtdq73nytGQnbTSuk-ly7dKR5pkircnzjeZHguubZjmkoldbYNJsqpe1_JTr8f3Q82UScrZZ3O20jpFPtDkFCvcaeSduwnTd-r6kEKMGltQ8KUb0fox40b8ZXZ66RHHuezJTFMfmHhTxuuqmk)]

You can read the original text and context of the resolution via the [Marxists Internet Archive](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHrOzAVg8GhcMLBYLV6JIUKbLCU4Um_hJhdWIe4SPyBFz07-R3qteNEk1tB-CtwaT4bCvf-G97mTS2cLoPt4mxUUiQ8eeY_jNB2ByafsVgjnNf458gct0Vc-YHS2_jYuhn93j2TLORdQuWFli8eSbfr1IE3DXp_AqVGpKE). d: THE RULE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The ban on factions was introduced in March 1921 at the Tenth Congress of the Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks) through the resolution "On Party Unity", proposed by Vladimir Lenin.' Key details (resolution, penalty, targets, context), consequences ('End of Internal Debate'; 'Path to Stalinism'), and a link to the Marxists Internet Archive text. Nine cards: Wikipedia, Reddit, Indybay (a DSA class on the ban, 2026-08-31), Quizlet, Alpha History, the Marxists Internet Archive, Brill, Seventeen Moments in Soviet History, WordPress.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the rule and its year, the Overview gives its name, congress, mover, terms, penalty, targets, context and consequences, and points to the primary text.
findings: THE RULE AND ITS PENALTY AT THE FIELD'S GRAIN. 'It authorized the Central Committee to use expulsion from the party as an extreme measure against any members, including its own, who engaged in factional activity.' The substance of Point 7 is carried; that Point 7 was secret, unpublished until January 1924, is not.

THE CONSEQUENCE #1725 DOCUMENTS. 'It effectively dismantled the Bolshevik tradition of open internal debate, platform voting, and free discussion before reaching a party decision.' and 'It later provided Joseph Stalin with the institutional mechanism to purge rival political blocs'. The composition states the conversion of critique into expulsion that #1725 reads in the rule.

THE ABSORPTION ON PAPER NOT CARRIED. The resolution itself called criticism necessary, ordered a discussion bulletin and promised that the Workers' Opposition's concerns would be 'tested in practice' (sources/party-unity.txt). #1725: the resolution 'absorbs the critique on paper and prohibits its organized form.' The composition gives the prohibition and leaves out the absorption, so the rule appears as plain suppression.

THE RULE IN A LIVE ORGANIZATION. The Indybay card records a DSA East Bay class on the ban (31 August 2026). The field is still reading the rule in a live organization; #1725's DSA case (R22, the 2028 endorsement fight) is the contemporary site.
analysis: A faithful, field-grain composition of a rule whose consequence it states plainly. What it omits is the half of the text that makes the rule a model of the corrupted sublation #1725 describes: critique acknowledged in the same document that dissolves its organized form.
per_note: Lenin and the Tenth Congress named; the Marxists Internet Archive and Wikipedia among the cards.
